system.name: WebPilot
system.one_liner: A multi-agent system that plans web tasks globally and executes each subtask with a tailored MCTS, using reflection to adapt.

content.variant_note: robot-avatar agents in a global zone and a local zone, four small trees for the MCTS phases, and two wedge-linked boxes that unroll them on a real web task
content.argues: Splitting web-task execution into a global plan refined by reflection and a local MCTS that explores and scores actions lets LLM agents handle uncertain web environments.
content.subject: two optimization zones of a web agent: robot agents, a task plan, four MCTS-phase trees and two zoomed examples

layout.arrangement_note: Two tinted zones side by side inside one outer frame: a grey Global Optimization zone at left (title at the bottom) and a pale green Local Optimization zone at right (title at the top right). In the local zone the agents and four trees sit on top and two large framed boxes below are tied to the RENE and DES trees by thin wedge lines. A six-arrow legend sits at the bottom of the global zone.

encoding.color_means: Zone tint: grey = global, pale green = local. Reflections are colour-coded to the legend arrows: peach = sibling reflection, pale green = child reflection, light blue = simulation reflection. Green bubbles = agent utterances; gold nodes in the MVB tree = backpropagated path; dark teal arrows = main flow.
encoding.line_style_means: Legend: solid grey-blue = state transition; thick dark-green dashed = reflection generation; peach dashed = sibling reflection; thin pale-green dashed = simulation; pale-green dashed = child reflection; thick light-blue dashed = simulation reflection.
encoding.shape_means: Robot with a prop = agent role; stack of rounded cards = task, plan or list; small circle-and-line tree = MCTS tree; speech bubble = utterance; thin wedge = zoom.
encoding.marker_means: Roman numerals order the global steps; HTD, RTA, GOS, RENE, DES, MVB are caption abbreviations; T and R symbols name subtasks and reflections.
encoding.emphasis: Two bold zone titles and the two large wedge-linked boxes; coloured reflection boxes stand out against the pale zones; no single contribution is highlighted.
reusable_patterns: two tinted zones (global and local) with bold zone titles inside one outer frame
robot avatar per role with a prop that hints at its job, reused inside the zoom box
four small trees, one per search phase, with the changed nodes highlighted, under a bracket from the agent that runs them
thin wedge from a tree to a framed box that unrolls it into page snapshots, reflections and a chat
legend of six dashed arrow styles whose colours are reused on the matching boxes
stacked rounded cards for task, plan and finished subtasks
a scoring chat that ends in a one-line formula (0.5 x 8 + 0.5 x 9 = 8.5)

lessons.what_to_learn: Give each agent role its own robot avatar with a prop, put two levels of the method in two tinted zones, and zoom the new search phases into framed boxes that show a real example. Reuse the legend arrow colours as the fill of the boxes they describe.
lessons.suits: Multi-agent LLM systems with a high-level planner and a low-level search or executor, where an example episode and several kinds of reflection must be shown.

sections: 1 LMU Munich (section label in the index; no paragraph mentions the figure)
evidence: the Global Optimization phase involves generating a high-level plan by breaking down tasks into manageable subtasks
the Local Optimization phase executes each subtask using a tailored MCTS designed for complex environments
GOS: Goal-Oriented Selection; RENE: Reflection-Enhanced Node Expansion; DES: Dynamic Evaluation and Simulation; MVB: Maximal Value Backpropagation

summary: WebPilot is a multi-agent system for web tasks that couples a global plan with a local Monte Carlo tree search. Figure 1 puts both on one canvas. At left, a grey Global Optimization zone shows cartoon-robot agents (Planner, Controller, Extractor) turning a task card into a plan, handing each subtask to the local side and refining the plan after reflection, along arrows numbered I to V. At right, a pale green Local Optimization zone has Verifier and Explorer agents acting on a web environment and four small trees (GOS, RENE, DES, MVB) for the MCTS phases. Two wedge-linked boxes show real page snapshots, colour-coded reflections and a chat in which an Appraiser scores an action 8 and a page 9, giving 8.5. A legend names six arrow styles.
summary_zh: WebPilot 是把全局规划与局部蒙特卡洛树搜索结合的多智能体网页任务系统。图中左侧灰色“全局优化”区由卡通机器人规划、控制并提取信息，右侧绿色“局部优化”区有验证者、探索者和四棵搜索树，下方两个放大框展示页面快照、彩色反思和评分对话。
notes: No paragraph mentions the figure, so roles rest on the caption, the abstract and the drawing. Which tree each zoom box belongs to (RENE for the left, DES for the right) is read from where the wedge lines start; the exact target of arrow II inside the local zone is not drawn. Treating the two titled zones as panels is a choice (the index says one panel). The drawn content spans beyond the canvas in the SVG, which does not change the printed figure.
